keywords.nuance: やはり is used when a result matches intuition, expectation, or a pattern already known. It can also soften confirmation.
keywords.example: やっぱり、彼は来ました。

commonPitfall.title: Common Pitfall
commonPitfall.body: やはり is close to やっぱり, but slightly more formal and often used in writing or neutral speech.

questions.prompt: やはり、彼は時間を守ります。
questions.hint: Natural confirmation based on known reliability.

questions.prompt: 最初は不安だった。やはり簡単でした。
questions.hint: A feeling gets revised by a better outcome.
questions.answer: At first I was worried, but it turned out to be easy, as expected.

questions.prompt: この店は静かでした。やはり落ち着いた雰囲気です。
questions.answer: This place was quiet. After all, it has a calm atmosphere.

questions.prompt: 新しい先生は優しい。やはり授業が聞きやすいです。
questions.hint: Use to confirm consistency from prior assumption.
questions.answer: The new teacher is kind; therefore, the class is easy to follow.

productionQuestions.prompt: As I expected, he is still very patient.
productionQuestions.hint: Use やはり to confirm a known trait.

referenceAnswers.answer: やはり、あの先生はとても我慢強いです。
やはり彼は相変わらず忍耐強いですね。
referenceAnswers.note: Same meaning with a natural colloquial flavor.

productionQuestions.prompt: I knew this place would be quiet, and it was.
productionQuestions.hint: Use やはり to confirm an expectation about place.

referenceAnswers.answer: やはり図書館は静かでした。
やはり予想どおり、ここはとても静かです。
referenceAnswers.note: Uses 予想どおり with same meaning.

productionQuestions.prompt: You see, it turned out to be difficult, as you said.

referenceAnswers.answer: やはり、これは難しかったです。
やはりあなたの言ったとおりでした。

productionQuestions.prompt: He kept coming on time, as expected.

referenceAnswers.answer: やはり彼は時間通りに来ています。
やはりいつも通り、時間通りです。
referenceAnswers.note: Conversational variant for daily habit confirmation.
